title: call-schema-sleuth-notes
content:
Evening lab notes — quick breadcrumb log for the function-call/structured-output issue observed in prod-like replay.

Context:
- Incident surfaced: user-facing assistant produced malformed tool calls intermittently when prompt length > 1200 tokens and response used streaming.
- Repro surface: happens in ~1/30 requests in our canary workload; higher when prefix cache warm and micro-batching enabled.
- Hypothesis: a race between streaming chunk flush and KV-cache pointer update leading to truncated JSON in final chunk OR the model emitting partial tokens that downstream parser misinterprets.

What I tried (commands + immediate results):
1) Local replay with exact inputs (replay-id 2026-03-09T22:14Z):
   - command: ./replay_tool --id 2026-03-09T22:14Z --env canary --streaming true --batch-size 8
   - result: reproduced 1/12 runs; output had trailing "\n}}" replaced by "\n}" (missing one brace), parser error: "JSONDecodeError: Unterminated object starting at line 1 column 234"

2) Disabled streaming on runtime (same replay):
   - command: ./replay_tool --id ... --streaming false
   - result: no malformed calls in 30 runs. Suggests streaming boundary interaction.

3) Inserted 100ms flush delay between chunks in runtime's stream sender:
   - patch: runtime/stream_sender.py add sleep(0.1) after chunk emit when content_type=="function_call"
   - result: failures dropped to 1/60. Not perfect but strongly correlated.

4) Binary search on batch-size: 1,2,4,8,16
   - observations: batch-size 1 never reproduces; 4-8 most common; 16 rare but when it hits, the malformed portion is earlier in token stream.

5) Model-level sanity check: run with deterministic sampling (temp=0.0) vs temp=0.7:
   - deterministic reduced variance but didn't eliminate malformed outputs. So token sampling is not sole cause.

Error snippets collected:
- "JSONDecodeError: Unterminated object starting at line 1 column 234"
- last chunks captured (raw):
  ...
  "tool": "web_search",
  "args": {"query": "openai function calling best practices"}
  }
  }
- expected end:
  }
  }
  ]
- Note: missing closing bracket for array in many samples, not always same location.

Hypotheses (ranked):
- H1: Streaming chunk coalescing/reassembly bug in the edge proxy that sometimes drops a single '}' when content-type is function_call and chunk boundaries align a specific way. (High plausibility; matches streaming toggle experiment.)
- H2: Runtime emits an extra chunk containing only whitespace/newline which downstream reassembler trims aggressively and accidentally drops boundary markers. (Medium plausibility; try inserting non-whitespace chunk.)
- H3: Model emits tokens with control characters that our UTF-8 sanitizer strips, collapsing braces. (Low plausibility; deterministic sampling test and direct token capture didn't show control chars.)
- H4: Batching KV cache race where pointer update and streaming flush cause a repeated token or missing token due to off-by-one in iterator. (Medium plausibility; correlates with batch-size signal.)

Quick triage plan / next steps:
- Reproduce more deterministically: run replay with deterministic seeds and with an instrumentation flag that logs raw chunk boundaries (pre- and post-proxy). Add checksums (CRC32) per chunk so we can detect loss/alteration in transit.
- Add a tiny non-whitespace sentinel at end of every chunk for function_call streams (e.g., "<END_CHUNK:seq>") and strip it in parser. If sentinel appears in final stitched string, we know reassembly is faithful.
- Audit edge proxy code path that handles 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' for special-casing content types. Look for any trim() calls or regex that could match '}}' patterns.
- Re-run with a patched stream_sender that emits a 0-width non-breaking space (U+00A0) at the end of each chunk and confirm parser behavior. If that prevents trimming, then whitespace-trimming was the culprit.
- Add post-assemble JSON-lint step in parser (lenient repair mode) that logs failures with byte offsets to S3 for offline triage. Do not auto-repair in prod.

Immediate experiment I want to run tonight (low-risk):
- Deploy canary runtime with sentinel addition and chunk CRC logging only in canary region. RTT overhead negligible, storage of logs to ephemeral bucket.
- Expected outcomes: either sentinel present (reassembler OK) or sentinel missing (proxy/transport lost it).

Notes to self:
- Don't rush into heuristics that silently autocorrect JSON; we should fail loudly so customers see consistent errors and we can correlate.
- If proxy trimming is root cause, change should be small: stop aggressive whitespace trimming for function_call streams.
- Revisit KV-cache pointer code after streaming bug fixed; race may still affect ordering in rare edge cases.

What to capture in logging (TODO checklist):
- [ ] raw chunk list as emitted by runtime (byte offsets)
- [ ] CRC32 per chunk
- [ ] reassembled payload length and CRC
- [ ] streaming session id + sequence number
- [ ] batch-size and kv-cache-seq during request
- [ ] model name + prompt length + sampling params

Slack breadcrumbs: #runtime-streaming thread has initial report (link in linked_artifacts). Pinged Priya for proxy pair-review.

If this turns into a durable fix: propose a small post-commit to add chunk checksums and optional sentinel toggles behind a feature flag (ff:stream_chunk_sentinels).

Misc oddities observed:
- Some malformed examples had duplicated 'args' keys: "args": {...}, "args": {...} which suggests merge-on-reassembly bug instead of drop-only. Keep an eye out for token duplication as well as deletion.
- One sample contained "\u0000" embedded in chunk boundary when captured from the agent; likely sanitizer insertion.

End of notes for now — will collect more after canary run.

If you pick this up: start with chunk CRC + sentinel experiment and attach a small harness to auto-run 200 replays overnight with streaming on/off permutations.

— Jordan
